dialogues.title: Dialogue 1
dialogues.setting: Mr. Ho invites Mr. Wong to his home for a meal

lines.speaker: Wong
lines.zh: 何先生，你太客气啦，煮咁多𩠌请我食饭。
lines.jp: ho4 sin1 saang1, nei5 taai3 haak3 hei3 laa1, zyu2 gam3 do1 sung3 cing2 ngo5 sik6 faan6
lines.en: Mr. Ho, you are very welcome, cook so much food to treat me

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 便饭啫，随便食喇。要唔要茶呀？
lines.jp: bin6 faan6 ze1, ceoi4 bin2 sik6 laa1. jiu3 m4 jiu3 caa4 aa3?
lines.en: It's nothing, eat as much as you like, do you want some tea?

lines.speaker: Wong
lines.zh: 唔要，唔该。何太太呢？佢喺边度呀？
lines.jp: m4 jiu3, m4 goi1. ho4 taai3 taai2 ne1? keoi5 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3?
lines.en: No, thanks. What about Mrs. Ho? Where is she?

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 佢喺厨房煮紧饭，唔使等佢啦。
lines.jp: keoi5 hai2 cyu4 fong2 zyu2 gan2 faan6, m4 sai2 dang2 keoi5 laa1
lines.en: She is cooking in the kitchen, no need to wait for her

lines.speaker: Wong
lines.zh: 何太太煮嘅𩠌真好食勒。好似酒楼嘅一样。何先生你有冇帮佢手呀？
lines.jp: ho4 taai3 taai2 zyu2 ge3 sung3 zan1 hou2 sik6 laak3. hou2 ci5 zau2 lau4 ge3 jat1 joeng6. ho4 sin1 saang1 nei5 jau5 mou5 bong1 keoi5 sau2 aa3?
lines.en: Mrs. Ho's cooking is really delicious, tastes like those from the restaurant. Did you help her Mr. Ho?

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 冇呀！
lines.jp: mou5 aa3!
lines.en: I didn't

lines.speaker: Wong
lines.zh: 何太太一定用咗好多时间预备呢餐饭勒。
lines.jp: ho4 taai3 taai2 jat1 ding6 jung6 zo2 hou2 do1 si4 gaan3 jyu6 bei6 ni1 caan1 faan6 laak3
lines.en: Mrs. Ho must have used a lot of time to prepare this meal

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 佢用咗半个钟头啫。
lines.jp: keoi5 jung6 zo2 bun3 go3 zung1 tau4 ze1
lines.en: She only used half an hour

lines.speaker: Wong
lines.zh: 只係半个钟头吖？我唔信。
lines.jp: zi2 hai6 bun3 go3 zung1 tau4 aa4? ngo5 m4 seon3
lines.en: Only half an hour? I don't believe you

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 係真架。啲𩠌都係佢去附近嘅酒楼买嘅。
lines.jp: hai6 zan1 gaa3. di1 sung3 dou1 hai6 keoi5 heoi3 fu6 gan6 ge3 zau2 lau4 maai5 ge3
lines.en: It's true! She bought these dish from the restaurant nearby

lines.speaker: Wong
lines.zh: 哦！
lines.jp: ngo5!
lines.en: Oh really!

dialogues.title: Dialogue 2
dialogues.setting: Mr. Ho tries to order a meal from a waiter

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 伙计，我想要一个汤，你地嘅汤新唔新鲜呀？
lines.jp: fo2 gei3, ngo5 soeng2 jiu3 jat1 go3 tong1, nei5 dei6 ge3 tong1 san1 m4 san1 sin1 aa3?
lines.en: Waiter, I want to order a soup, is your soup fresh?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.zh: 先生，你要个牛肉汤喇。好新鲜架。
lines.jp: sin1 saang1, nei5 jiu3 go3 ngau4 juk6 tong1 laa1. hou2 san1 sin1 gaa3
lines.en: Mr. you should order a beef soup, it's very fresh

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 好，我就要个牛肉汤。主菜有乜嘢好介绍呀？
lines.jp: hou2, ngo5 zau6 jiu3 go3 ngau4 juk6 tong1. zyu2 coi3 jau5 mat1 je5 hou2 gaai3 siu6 aa3?
lines.en: Good, I'll get a beef soup. What do you recommend for the main dish?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.zh: 龙虾饭喇，好好味架。如果你要呢个饭，我地送生果沙律俾你。
lines.jp: lung4 haa1 faan6 laa1, hou2 hou2 mei6 gaa3. jyu4 gwo2 nei5 jiu3 ni1 go3 faan6, ngo5 dei6 sung3 saang1 gwo2 saa1 leot2 bei2 nei5
lines.en: Lobster rice. It's very delicious. If you order this rice, I'll give you fruit salad for free

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 点解送生果沙律呀？
lines.jp: dim2 gaai2 sung3 saang1 gwo2 saa1 leot2 aa3?
lines.en: Why free fruit salad?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.zh: 因为我地嘅厨房昨日整左太多，今日仲有唔少，所以就送俾你食喇。
lines.jp: jan1 wai6 ngo5 dei6 ge3 cyu4 fong2 zok6 jat6 zing2 zo2 taai3 do1, gam1 jat6 zung6 jau5 m4 siu2, so2 ji5 zau6 sung3 bei2 nei5 sik6 laa1
lines.en: Because our kitchen made too much yesterday, still have some leftover today therefore we gave you for free

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 你地昨日整嘅生果沙律今日俾我食，你识唔识做生意架？
lines.jp: nei5 dei6 zok3 jat6 zing2 ge3 saang1 gwo2 saa1 leot2 gam1 jat6 bei2 ngo5 sik6, nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 zou6 saang1 ji3 gaa3?
lines.en: You gave me yesterday's fruit salad? Do you know how to run a business?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.zh: 先生，你唔好嬲。我再送今朝早整嘅甜品俾你，好吗？仲係好好味架。
lines.jp: sin1 saang1, nei5 m4 hou2 nau1. ngo5 zoi3 sung3 gam1 ziu1 zou2 zing2 ge3 tim4 ban2 bei2 nei5, hou2 maa3? zung6 hai6 hou2 hou2 mei6 gaa3
lines.en: Mr. don't be mad. I'll give you this morning's desert as well, ok? It's still very delicious

lines.speaker: Ho
lines.zh: 乜嘢话？昨日嘅生果沙律：今朝早嘅甜品！你当我係垃圾桶吖！
lines.jp: mat1 je5 waa2? zok6 jat6 ge3 saang1 gwo2 saa1 leot2: gam1 ziu1 zou2 ge3 tim4 ban2! nei5 dong3 ngo5 hai6 laap6 saap6 tung2 aa4!
lines.en: What the heck. Yesterday's fruit salad? This morning's desert? You thought I'm a trash can!

grammar.title: cing2 to invite
grammar.summary: cing2 means please (Unit 3) and also to invite.
grammar.body: In Unit 3 we saw that cing2 means please. It has another meaning of to invite.

examples.jp: keoi5 cing2 ngo5 heoi3 keoi5 nguk1 kei5
examples.en: He invites me to go to his home

grammar.title: Lonely verbs
grammar.summary: Some verbs (sik6, zyu2) feel incomplete without an object, so the all-purpose object faan6 is supplied.
grammar.body:
Some verbs feel incomplete if they have no object, so Cantonese will supply an all-purpose object to comfort their loneliness! In English we have no problem with saying he is eating, but the Cantonese verb sik6 is unhappy on its own and if it is not specified what he is eating then the all purpose object faan6 rice will be added.
zyu2 to cook is another verb which takes faan6 for want of anything more definite and we will meet other such verbs and other all purpose objects in later units.

grammar.title: Adverbs of place
grammar.summary: The adverb saying where an action happens comes before or after the subject, but always before the verb.
grammar.body: The adverb which says where an action is happening comes either before or after the subject depending on the sense, but in any case it always comes before the verb.

examples.jp: hai2 se2 zi6 lau4 nei5 jau5 mou5 bat1 aa3?
examples.en: Have you got a pen in the office?

grammar.title: Two new verb endings: gan2 and zo2
grammar.summary: …gan2 marks an action going on at the time; …zo2 marks a completed action, usually backed up by laak3.
grammar.body:
…gan2 is tagged onto a verb to emphasize that the action is actually going on at the time.
…zo2 is tagged onto a verb in the same way to show that the action has been completed. Usually the particle laak3 is added at the end of the sentence to back it up.

examples.jp: wong4 sin1 saang1 tai2 gan2 ji1 saang1
examples.en: Mr. Wong is seeing the doctor

examples.jp: keoi5 tai2 zo2 ji1 saang1 laak3
ngo5 maai5 zo2 mei5 gwok3 ce1 laak3

grammar.title: An irregular verb: jiu3/sai2
grammar.summary: To need to is jiu3 but its negative is m4 sai2 (question sai2 m4 sai2); when jiu3 means to want, the negative is m4 jiu3 (question jiu3 m4 jiu3).
grammar.body:
To need to is jiu3 but not to need to is m4 sai2.
However, when jiu3 means to want its negative is m4 jiu3.
The question form for to need to is sai2 m4 sai2.
The question form for to want is jiu3 m4 jiu3.

examples.en: We need to wait for her

examples.jp: ngo5 dei6 m4 sai2 dang2 keoi5 laa1
examples.en: We don't need to wait for her
I need to buy a car
I don't need to buy a car

examples.jp: ngo5 dei6 sai2 m4 sai2 dang2 keoi5 aa3?
examples.en: Do we need to wait for her?

examples.jp: nei5 jiu3 m4 jiu3 faan6 aa3?

grammar.title: Another use of ge3
grammar.summary: Besides possession, ge3 links a descriptive phrase (adjectives) to a noun.
grammar.body: We saw in unit 2 that ge3 shows possession: ngo5 ge3 ce1 my car. It also is used to link a descriptive phrase (adjectives) to a noun.

examples.en: The person who is buying an expensive pen
The house that he lives in

grammar.title: Adjectives
grammar.summary: Attributive adjectives modify nouns (with ge3); predicative adjectives drop hai6 and usually take hou2, or another modifier such as gei2, gam3, taai3 or gau3 (saai3).
grammar.body:
Attributive adjectives modify the nouns.
Adjectives can be modified by hou2 'very' or zeoi3 'most'.
Predicative adjectives are used to state that something has a certain property. The verb hai6 'to be' is not used, but instead the adverb hou2 is usually included.
Other modifiers such as gei2 'quite' and gam3 'so' can appear in place of hou2.

examples.jp: hou2 kan4 lik6 ge3 hok6 saang1
zeoi3 nin4 hing1 ge3 bok3 si6

examples.en: The air tickets are quite cheap

examples.jp: nei5 go3 sau2 tai4 din6 nou5 gam3 gwai3
examples.en: Your laptop computer is so expensive
The string is (more than) long enough

grammar.title: Reduplicated adjectives
grammar.summary: Reduplicating an adjective with the suffix -dei2 means 'rather…'; the repeated syllable changes to high rising tone unless it is already tone 1 or 2. Not used with hou2 or gei2.
grammar.body:
Another strategy to modify the meaning of an adjective is reduplication together with the suffix -dei2.
Note the change to a high rising tone on the repeated syllable: this happens in all cases except where the original tone is high level as in din1 din1 dei2 or already high rising as in fu2 fu2 dei2.
Used to qualify the force of an adjective.
Note these forms are not used together with hou2 or other modifiers such as gei2 'quite': not *ni1 go3 gaau3 sau6 hou2 din1 din1 dei2; not *go3 wu6 si6 gei2 fei4 fei2 dei2.

examples.en: The street is a bit wet

examples.jp: ngo5 gok3 dak1 mun6 mun2 dei2
ni1 go3 gaau3 sau6 din1 din1 dei2
go3 wu6 si6 fei4 fei2 dei2

grammar.title: Have you done it?
grammar.summary: To ask if an action has been completed use jau5 mou5 + verb; answer with jau5 (yes) or mou5 (no).
grammar.body:
To ask if an action has been completed, Cantonese (like English) can use the verb to have (jau5).
The answer is a simple jau5 yes or mou5 no.

examples.jp: nei5 taai3 taai2 jau5 mou5 faan1 heoi3 aa3?
keoi5 jau5 mou5 sik6 faan6 aa3?

grammar.title: Plurals and quantities with di1
grammar.summary: di1 啲 refers to an unspecified number of countable items or a quantity of an uncountable substance.
grammar.body:
Referring to an unspecified number of countable items.
Referring to quantities of uncountable substances.

examples.en: The oranges are nice and sweet

examples.jp: ngo5 heoi3 taam3 di1 pang4 jau5
examples.en: I'm going to visit some friends

examples.jp: keoi5 di1 tung4 si6 taai3 mong4

examples.en: The water is not hot enough

examples.jp: ngo5 jiu3 maai5 di1 sin1 naai5
examples.en: I need to buy some fresh milk

grammar.title: Compare the classifiers
grammar.summary: Classifiers with ni1/go2/numbers vs. di1 for uncounted plurals; a definite noun at the start of a sentence takes its classifier where English uses 'the'.
grammar.body:
Compare the classifiers in the following.
When a sentence starts with a definite noun (the pen, the food, the Americans) Cantonese uses the appropriate classifier where English uses the.

examples.jp: di1 mei5 gwok3 jan4 lai4 m4 lai4 aa3?

grammar.title: The adverb dou1 again
grammar.summary: dou1 means also, all or both; it comes immediately before the verb and after the noun it refers to.
grammar.body: In unit 1 we met the adverb dou1 meaning also. Other meanings are all and both. dou1 must come immediately before a verb and it obeys a further rule that it must come after the noun it refers to. Note carefully the placing of dou1 in the following.

examples.jp: nei5 jau5 bat1, keoi5 dou1 jau5 bat1
examples.en: You have a pen, and he has too

examples.jp: wong4 sin1 saang1 wong4 siu2 ze2 dou1 faan1 zo2 se2 zi6 lau4 laak3
examples.en: Both Mr. and Miss Wong have gone to the office

examples.jp: go2 loeng5 go3 jing1 gwok3 jan4 dou1 m4 soeng2 sik6 faan6
examples.en: Neither of those two British people wants to eat

grammar.title: To give
grammar.summary: sung3 (to present, make a gift) usually appears with bei2 (to give to): sung3 X bei2 Y. bei2 alone more commonly means to give to, to hand over to.
grammar.body:
Sung3 means to present, to make a gift. It usually appears with bei2… which itself means to give, to give to. The word order for giving a present to someone is a comfortable one for an English speaker.
bei2… is sometimes used on its own to mean to present, but it is more commonly found meaning just to give to, to hand over to.

examples.jp: keoi5 sung3 jat1 zi1 bat1 bei2 ngo5
examples.en: He gives a pen to me (as a gift)

examples.jp: keoi5 bei2 jat1 zi1 bat1 ngo5
examples.en: He hands a pen to me/hands me a pen

grammar.title: Shortcuts
grammar.summary: Common phrases are shortened: gam1 jat6 ziu1 zou2 > gam1 ziu1, wong4 sin1 saang1 > wong4 saang1, m4 hou2 > mai5 (ruder).
grammar.body:
Cantonese is a lively quick-fire language and speakers often find ways of shortening phrases which seem to them to be too tediously long. Here is a list of shortened forms of phrases which you have met so far.
M4 hou2 / Mai5: both mean don't but mai5 is a bit ruder because it is so abrupt sounding.

examples.jp: gam1 jat6 ziu1 zou2 = gam1 ziu1 zou2 = gam1 ziu1
zok6 jat6 ziu1 zou2 = zok6 ziu1 zou2 = zok6 ziu1

examples.en: Don't (mai5 is a bit ruder because it is so abrupt sounding)

grammar.title: Don't
grammar.summary: To tell someone not to do something use m4 hou2 (it's not good to…) or nei5 m4 hou2 (it's not good that you should…).
grammar.body: To tell someone not to do something, Cantonese uses m4 hou2 it's not good to… to nei5 m4 hou2 it's not good that you should…

notes.title: Rice
notes.body: Rice is the staple food of the south China and is much appreciated as the superior grain in the north too. Not surprisingly, rice figures large in Chinese culture: it is offered in religious sacrifices to the ancestors; it is thrown over newly-weds to bring fertility to them; bags of it are laid on babies' stomaches to comfort them and stop them crying; the language is full sayings about it: English has only one the word rice but Cantonese has many words for it. Faan6 means rice only when it is cooked rice. There are different words for rice when growing, rice when harvested but not husked, rice husked but not cooked, and rice cooked into a gruel, as well as yet other terms for different kinds of rice such as red rice, glutinous rice and non-glutinous rice.
